issues.legal_issue: Participants who jointly facilitate a killing may be convicted of murder on the basis of shared intention inferred from their coordinated conduct.
material_facts: After a quarrel, several accused arrived together, some carrying sticks and another carrying a spear.
One accused directed the others to kill the victim.
The accused with sticks moved to prevent the victim from escaping, while the spear-wielding accused fatally stabbed him.
The group had acted together in a continuing dispute and their conduct enabled the killing.
issues.conclusion: The murder convictions with the aid of the shared-intention principle were affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, shared intention may be inferred from concerted conduct and the circumstances of the attack. Conduct that blocks a victim’s escape while another participant carries out a killing, together with an order to kill and coordinated arrival armed for the encounter, supported the finding of shared intention. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_joint_murder_conviction and group_member_directed_killing and participants_arrived_together_armed and participants_blocked_victims_escape and principal_participant_killed_victim

predicates.appeal_from_joint_murder_conviction: The accused appealed a conviction for murder based on acting together with another participant.
predicates.group_member_directed_killing: A member of the group directed the others to kill the victim.
predicates.participants_arrived_together_armed: The participants arrived together, with members of the group carrying weapons.
predicates.participants_blocked_victims_escape: Some participants acted to prevent the victim from escaping.
predicates.principal_participant_killed_victim: One participant inflicted the fatal injuries on the victim.

issues.definition: When a murder appeal involves a group that arrived armed, was directed to kill, blocked the victim’s escape, and included the person who killed the victim, the joint murder conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for a jointly committed assault cannot be maintained where the alleged victim did not testify and the alleged injuries were not proved.
material_facts: The accused were also convicted of assaulting a person who had tried to intervene.
The alleged victim did not testify, and his injuries were not proved.
issues.conclusion: The assault convictions were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court concluded that, in the circumstances, the convictions under Sections 323 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code could and should be set aside because the alleged victim did not testify and his injuries were not proved. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_joint_assault_conviction: The accused appealed a conviction for an assault allegedly committed together.
predicates.alleged_victim_did_not_testify: The person said to have been assaulted did not testify at trial.
predicates.alleged_injuries_not_proved: The injuries said to have resulted from the assault were not proved.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a joint assault conviction and the alleged victim did not testify and the alleged injuries were not proved, the conviction is set aside.
